summary: The patch fixes the reported `.Z`/`.br` cases but does so with fragile `filename.endswith()` string matching instead of extending the adjacent encoding map dict that already holds the analogous gzip/bzip2/xz entries. Functionally correct for the report, but a Django maintainer would reject this approach in favor of the trivial idiomatic fix.

issues.description: The `mimetypes.guess_type` call already yields an `encoding` ('compress' for .Z, 'br' for .br). The correct, idiomatic fix is to add `"br": "application/x-brotli", "compress": "application/x-compress"` to the existing encoding->content_type dict immediately above. Re-deriving the extension via `filename.endswith()` ignores the value mimetypes already computed and is the wrong abstraction; a maintainer would request the encoding-map approach.

Special-casing two literal suffixes (`.Z`, `.br`) does not generalize and bypasses the encoding-handling mechanism. Future encodings would need yet more endswith branches rather than one dict entry, and the suffix check is case-sensitive (won't match e.g. `.BR`), unlike the mimetypes encoding detection.
Uses single-quoted string literals ('.Z', '.br') while Django is black-formatted with double quotes throughout; this would be reflowed/flagged by Django's enforced black/style checks.
Adds an if/elif/else that duplicates content-type resolution logic right after the encoding map is built, making the block harder to read than a single dict-based assignment.
